newsitem.title: IRAN: Pakistan minister to discuss Afghan crisis in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan minister to discuss Afghan crisis in Iran.

text.p: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Sahibzada Yaqoob Khan is due to hold talks in Tehran on Wednesday to try to coordinate policy towards Afghanistan with Iranian leaders.
The three-day talks would centre on "attaining a durable peace in Afghanistan," Pakistan's ambassador to Tehran Khaled Mahmoud told the official Iranian news agency IRNA.
Khan is scheduled to meet Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati and Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq Nouri during his visit.
He left Pakistan for Iran on Tuesday while U.N.-sponsored peace talks between rival Afghan factions, which started on Monday, were in full swing.
Iran and Pakistan hold contrasting views of the Taleban Islamic movement, viewed with deep suspicions in Tehran, but have sought to contain their differences by maintaining a dialogue on Afghanistan.
Both countries say they support U.N. peace efforts and deny favouring any one Afghan faction over another.
Tehran has previously charged Pakistan with backing the Taleban, which seized Kabul in September.
"We in Iran expect him (Khan) to clear the air and declare Pakistan's official Afghan policy," the English-language Iran News daily paper said in its Wednesday's editorial.

"Taleban not only deprived several ethnic communities of that country of their fundamental rights but also misrepresented true Islam through whimsical interpretations of this great religion," Iran News said.
